items.text:
Can't rotate the player camera, can rotate the ship camera! Pardon my French but, what???

"Undock, rotate, re-dock" says the developer. 

That would be splendid, were I not too poor to pay the undocking fee. 

I've had Ostranauts on my wish list for a while and I was hesitant to pull the trigger on buying it, I was pleasantly surprised to see the game come out of early access and thought sure why not. I've nearly managed to just about finish the introductory tutorial but I'm just going to have to refund this, I've seen the reviews, and having had a little taste of it myself I can already feel the game sink its hooks in. 

There's no worse feeling than finding yourself a victim of the sunk cost fallacy, that the book you really wanted to enjoy isn't going to be reissued or the disappointing series you binged isn't going to be re-shot, and the time you gave it is well and truly gone. There is something to be said for how early access is such a wonderful approach to game development, it puts players and developers in touch with one another that can make the time you spent playing or creating the game like such a rewarding investment. 

But something here seems to have gone very wrong with Ostranauts that has me questioning the developers intentions. Now I don't know a lick about game design, nor do I consider camera rotation in a top down game an essential, but in Ostranauts camera rotation is relative to the orientation of the player owned ship, and where you dock on a station can change the camera. This doesn't materially change how you play the game but it means that if there's decal text in a station you want to read you'll need to crane your neck or rotate your camera, simple, right?

Part of the games difficulty, amongst its many systems and menus to navigate, is the banal nickel and diming the player is expected to keep on top of. I've just returned from my tutorial expedition to the home station to find that not only was my initial haul paltry, it's not even enough to cover the overhead surcharge for me to leave the station. No problem, I'll see if I can follow the station signage to somewhere that I might be able to scrounge up the remainder. 

Now, granted, on the Ostranauts Discussion post "Camera Rotation not working!?" the developer self deprecatingly remarks that it is hacky design that camera rotation is locked to the ship and that were the game not developed in early access, it would be done differently. But for a 1.0 full release? Yeah, it's hacky design. People have a lot to say on how companies impose outrageous convenience fees, how microtransactions ruin games, but it wasn't until Ostranauts had I ever been charged a red cent to rotate my camera.

Good will is a valuable currency, and I'd have more of it to spend had I bought this in Early Access. Have a read through the other reviews if you're interested, there are players who have sunk hundreds of hours into this game wishing it didn't feel like such a waste. I feel like ive done myself a favour, and you will be too, by spending your time and money elsewhere.
items.text_zh:
不能旋转玩家摄像机，却能旋转飞船摄像机！恕我直言，什么？？？

“脱离对接，旋转，重新对接”，开发者如是说。

那倒是妙极了，要不是我穷得付不起脱离对接费的话。

Ostranauts在我的愿望清单上待了一阵子了，我一直犹豫要不要下手买，结果惊喜地看到游戏脱离抢先体验正式发售，心想当然可以试试。我差点就快把入门教程打完了，但我还是只能退款，我看过那些评测，而且自己稍微尝了一口，就已经能感觉到这游戏把钩子扎进来了。

没有什么比发现自己成了沉没成本谬误的受害者更糟的感觉了——你真心想享受的那本书不会重新出版，你一口气刷完的那部令人失望的剧集不会重拍，而你付出的时间已经真真切切地一去不返。抢先体验作为游戏开发的一种方式有多美妙，确实值得一说，它让玩家和开发者彼此接触，能让你花在玩游戏或做游戏上的时间像是一笔很有回报的投资。

但Ostranauts这里似乎有什么地方出了大问题，让我开始质疑开发者的意图。我对游戏设计一窍不通，也不认为俯视视角游戏里的摄像机旋转是什么必需品，但在Ostranauts里，摄像机旋转是相对于玩家所拥有飞船的朝向的，而你在空间站上停靠的位置会改变摄像机。这并不会实质性地改变你玩游戏的方式，但这意味着如果空间站里有你想读的贴花文字，你就得扭着脖子或者旋转摄像机，很简单，对吧？

这游戏的难度，一部分就来自它那众多需要摸索的系统和菜单，另一部分则在于玩家被期望时刻盯住的那种琐碎的锱铢必较。我刚从教程远征回到母站，发现我不但初次收获少得可怜，甚至还不够支付我离开空间站的管理附加费。没问题，我看看能不能顺着空间站的标识找到某个地方，让我能凑出剩下的钱。

当然，在Ostranauts讨论帖“摄像机旋转不工作！？”里，开发者自嘲地说，摄像机旋转锁定在飞船上是一种拼凑式的设计，如果游戏不是在抢先体验中开发的，做法会不一样。但这是1.0正式版？是啊，这就是拼凑式设计。人们对公司强加离谱的便利费、对微交易毁掉游戏有很多话要说，但直到Ostranauts，我才第一次因为旋转摄像机而被收了一分钱。

善意是一种宝贵的货币，如果我是在抢先体验期间买的，我会有更多善意可花。如果你有兴趣，去读读其他评测吧，有些玩家在这游戏里投入了数百小时，却希望它别感觉这么浪费。我觉得我帮了自己一个忙，你把时间和钱花在别处，也会是在帮你自己。

items.text:
BAD
-Text at times is impossible to read from tutorials
-Need at least 5k cash minimum to progress anywhere in the game but game gives you about 100 and a poor tutorial for you to figure out how to scrap for money, money that you dont get enough of and end up debugging
cash in anyways 
-Korean/English text litters your view making everything feel cluttered and messy
-flying the ship is cool but there is constant issue with the camera moving and not sticking to the ship despite my settings being set to follow ship, think it has something to do with the clunky autonav which requires a ridiculous distance to work
-holding left alt just highlights whats usable, doesnt tell you WHAT they are so in messy maps where all textures look like a frat house its like playing a game of where's waldo to find something
-incredibly unoptimized, lags hard in certain areas despite having a 3060 which should be more than capable of running this)
-5 year early access so i dont think they are fixing anything anytime soon, buy when it goes on sale.

GOOD
-pretty original idea
-concepts are pretty intuitive
-rich text based story
items.text_zh:
差评
-教程里的文字有时根本没法看
-想在游戏里取得任何进展至少需要5000现金，但游戏只给你大约100，而且教程很烂，让你自己想办法拆解废料换钱，而钱你根本赚不够，最后只能靠调试
无论如何都要现金
-韩文/英文文本布满你的视野，让一切感觉杂乱又凌乱
-驾驶飞船很酷，但相机不断出问题，不会固定在飞船上，尽管我的设置已经设为跟随飞船，我觉得这跟笨拙的自动导航有关，它需要荒谬的距离才能工作
-按住左Alt只会高亮可用的东西，不会告诉你它们是什么，所以在所有纹理看起来都像兄弟会宿舍的杂乱地图里，就像在玩找沃尔多游戏一样找东西
-优化极差，在某些区域严重卡顿，尽管我有3060，按理说运行这个绰绰有余）
-抢先体验5年了，所以我觉得他们短期内不会修任何东西，等打折再买。

好评
-想法相当原创
-概念相当直观
-丰富的文本驱动故事

items.text:
[i]Very[/i] unfriendly tutorial. I was excited my the idea of this game but there's so much visual noise immediately. My feedback would be to lock away some of the complexity and drip feed it to a new player. 

The concept is so nice and I imagine once you have a deep understanding of everything, it's probably enjoyable. 
But most new players will likely be put off by the first 30 minutes, as I was. 

I felt there was a depth of play available but it was concealed behind a lot of frustrating elements.

Couple of other bits of feedback. The click to select on the Nav Station doesn't feel user friendly. Click and drag should be considered movement, clicking to move the frame was confusing. Especially as it kept locking the camera back to the crosshairs. It's also really not apparent which is your ship to a new player, in relation to anything. 
Names of things are also hidden if scrolled out, so it took a while to realise ONKG (sp) was hidden under a stack of names of things. Could be solved through a stack display accessible through hover or click of the mouse.
items.text_zh:
[i]非常[/i]不友好的教程。我本来对这款游戏的想法很兴奋，但立刻就有太多视觉噪音。我的反馈是，应该把一些复杂性锁起来，并逐步喂给新玩家。 

这个概念非常好，我想一旦你对一切都有了深入理解，它大概会很好玩。 
但大多数新玩家很可能会像我一样，被前30分钟劝退。 

我觉得游戏中有可玩的深度，但它被许多令人沮丧的元素掩盖了。

还有几点其他反馈。在导航站上点击选择感觉并不友好。点击并拖动应该被视为移动，点击来移动框架令人困惑。尤其是它还总是把镜头锁回准星。对于新玩家来说，也真的很不明显哪艘是你的飞船，以及它与其他任何东西的关系。 
如果缩小视野，物品名称也会被隐藏，所以我过了一阵子才意识到ONKG（原文如此）被藏在一堆物品名称下面。也许可以通过悬停或鼠标点击访问的堆叠显示来解决。

observations.evidence: Especially as it kept locking the camera back to the crosshairs.
observations.evidence_zh: 尤其是因为它总是把镜头锁回准星。
